problem: Source suppression publishes active before native window activation/post-authorization completes. Queued input can therefore start full authority queries on the same channel and writes on the same pipe before the actual activation ACK.
change: Hold the existing ordered sender on one activation-epoch fence before any input authority/wire work. Release only after the operation and its exact successful ACK write both complete. Keep suppression and the bounded/coalescing input queue active during this wait.

evidence.originalOrderingReproduced: Removing the sender fence makes the regression fail because input starts full authority/wire work before activation completion.
evidence.causalLimit: This proves an avoidable concurrency dependency, not that all of the physical 345.372ms response wait is caused by it. Native execution, authorization and reply scheduling still require physical comparison.

verificationFocus: A pending activation starts zero input proofs/writes and its real ACK precedes every queued input packet.
1000 queued relative move deltas survive coalescing, followed by exact key-down/key-up order and fresh per-frame authority.
Negative activation, epoch change, replaced fence and obsolete session input never reach the pipe.
Operation/owner cancellation releases a waiting sender without requiring activation completion.
Native failure, ACK failure and uncertain retirement keep their existing failure/cleanup classification.
remainingLimitations: A native activation or independent authority/OS call can still be slow; no timeout or security boundary is weakened.
A sufficiently long activation plus discrete-event flood can still exhaust the existing bounded input queue.
Existing detailed-profile retention is at most 12 attempts per 120-second window; use a new window to distinguish later dwell tests.

localValidation.raceFixtureRepair: Existing expired-authentication test read Authority.closed without its mutex. It now observes pending query ownership under queryMu and reads closed only after joined retirement under authority.mu.
